### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 107be283f030242a7803848ae31a1ec11e9891dc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b8c078a61aab6b8c1175ac28cb0a5869338a486e` — the merge of head `a4a79ea320ddb1df2876917b63848aa94a79bd8f` into base `107be283f030242a7803848ae31a1ec11e9891dc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b8c078a61aab6b8c1175ac28cb0a5869338a486e && git checkout b8c078a61aab6b8c1175ac28cb0a5869338a486e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 107be283f030242a7803848ae31a1ec11e9891dc a4a79ea320ddb1df2876917b63848aa94a79bd8f && git checkout -B drift-repro 107be283f030242a7803848ae31a1ec11e9891dc && git merge --no-ff a4a79ea320ddb1df2876917b63848aa94a79bd8f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 107be283f030242a7803848ae31a1ec11e9891dc
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d68dd29fc31de1930c00e64ae550826cdc4e70d7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts, packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`getPublicConfig()`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts (the `/config` route), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/public-feature-registry.test.ts, packages/types/src/env.ts (`resolveTenancyPosture`), ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs. Remainder of the diff (changeset, regenerated `authorable-surface/api.json` and `content/docs/references/api/auth-endpoints.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set widens, nine keys, all optional, no defaults** — right. `AuthFeaturesConfigSchema` (a plain `z.object`, so unknown keys were stripped) now declares `multiOrgEnabled`, `degradedTenancy`, `oidcProvider`, `deviceAuthorization`, `admin` as `z.boolean().optional()`, `tenancyPosture` as `TenancyPostureSchema.optional()`, `audiencePosture` as `z.enum(AUDIENCE_POSTURES).optional()`, `termsUrl` / `privacyUrl` as `z.string().optional()`. Every payload accepted on `main` is accepted unchanged (CONTROL test: absent keys stay absent).
- **Each declared type matches what the producer serves** — right, read on `main` in `auth-manager.ts` `getPublicConfig()` (the one `features` literal; both `/auth/config` routes, plugin-auth `auth-plugin.ts:3103` and the hono adapter `index.ts:988`, serve it and only refine `sso`):
  - `multiOrgEnabled = postureEnforcesWall(tenancyPosture)` → boolean.
  - `tenancyPosture = this.config.getTenancy?.()?.posture ?? resolveTenancyPosture()` → `TenancyPosture` on both arms (`TenancyService.posture: TenancyPosture`; `resolveTenancyPosture(): TenancyPosture`, which normalises the legacy `multi` to `isolated` before returning), the exact vocabulary of `TenancyPostureSchema` (`single|group|isolated`).
  - `audiencePosture = this.getAudience().posture` → `ResolvedAudience.posture: AudiencePosture`, coerced to `invite_only` when the raw value is off-vocabulary, the exact vocabulary of `AUDIENCE_POSTURES` (`invite_only|email_domain|open`).
  - `degradedTenancy = tenancy?.degraded ?? false` → boolean (`TenancyService.degraded: boolean`).
  - `oidcProvider = resolveOidcProviderEnabled(pluginConfig)` → declared `: boolean`.
  - `deviceAuthorization = pluginConfig.deviceAuthorization ?? false` → `AuthPluginConfigSchema.deviceAuthorization: z.boolean()`.
  - `admin = pluginConfig.admin ?? resolveScimEnabled(pluginConfig)` → `z.boolean().optional()` ?? `: boolean`.
  - `termsUrl` / `privacyUrl` → `resolveLegalUrl()` returns `string | undefined` (trimmed env value, default page, or `undefined` on an explicit empty string) and the key is spread in only when defined, so `z.string().optional()` with no URL validation is the honest type.
- **The nine names are the served names, unchanged** — right; the regenerated `authorable-surface/api.json` adds exactly nine `api/AuthFeaturesConfig:*` rows with those spellings and nothing else moves there. `api-surface` does not move (no export added).
- **Served ≡ registry ≡ schema now closes through the registry** — right. plugin-auth's drift guard (`public-feature-registry.test.ts`) holds served boolean keys ≡ `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURE_NAMES` and served non-boolean keys ⊆ `PUBLIC_AUTH_CONFIG_NON_FLAG_KEYS`; the new spec pin holds declared keys minus `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES_NOT_ADVERTISED` ≡ `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURE_NAMES` + `PUBLIC_AUTH_CONFIG_NON_FLAG_KEYS` in both directions, and that each tombstone stays declared. A re-advertised retired key now fails the pin until it leaves the tombstone list, which is the right ratchet.
- **New module edges** `api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts → security/tenancy-posture.ts`, `→ system/auth-config.zod.ts` — right; both import only `zod` (+ `lazySchema`), no cycle, and `api/*.zod.ts` already imports from `../security/` and `../system/` (`auth.zod.ts`, `dispatcher.zod.ts`, `plugin-rest-api.zod.ts`, `protocol.zod.ts`).
- **Top-level `devSeedAdmin` stays undeclared** — judged under ③.
- Check-runs on the head, read complete (65 runs): 57 success, 8 skipped (`Lint UI`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix)`, `Temporal Conformance`, `18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)`, `Schedule gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, none of which this diff reaches), 0 failures. Green among them: `Build Core`, all eight `Test Core` shards, `Type Check · source / consumer / workspace / debt ledger`, `Type Check UI`, every `Lint ·` family, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was run locally.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29473-auth-config-features-served-keys.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`; PR body carries the same two lines. Matches what the diff publishes: nine new optional keys on a published response schema, nothing narrowed, no export change.
- **`Metadata-protocol: added` over the claim's `none` — right, the dev's deviation stands.** `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (ruling A, "where the ratchets can SEE a protocol change, a declared `none` over it is refused") lists `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` in `PROTOCOL_BASELINE_ROOTS`; this diff moves `authorable-surface/api.json`, so `none` is refused by the gate and `added` with `minor` is the only declaration it accepts. It is also the precedent on this very schema (`sso` landed under `added` in PR #29455). The claim's `none` was a reading made before the build moved the shard; the seat's claim line is superseded, not contradicted, and the PR body says why. `Check Changeset` on the head is green.
- `Clause-②:` line: `yes (widening)`, one arm from the closed pair, well-formed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`devSeedAdmin`, open question A/B → A (keep undeclared), agreed.** Read on `main`: `auth-manager.ts:4634` builds it only when `NODE_ENV === 'development'` AND `devSeedResult` is set, and `auth-plugin.ts` sets `devSeedResult` only from `maybeSeedDevAdmin`'s own `NODE_ENV==='development'` gate, so it is dev-only by construction, and it carries `{ email, password }` in clear. Its one reader, `LoginPage.tsx:210`, casts the raw `cfg` and never parses through `GetAuthConfigResponseSchema`, so no consumer loses it. Declaring it (B) would put a password-bearing field on the published contract and the generated reference for a value no production deployment serves. The TSDoc block on `GetAuthConfigResponseSchema` records the ruling where the next reader of the schema looks, without feeding the reference page. The card's "or rule it out as dev-only" arm is taken, with reasons. No escalation.
- Deviation "Metadata-protocol added, claim said none": answered under ②, right.
- Deviation "Clause-② spelled `yes (widening)`": the claim line said `yes`; `(widening)` is the correct arm for a new optional key, fine.
- Deviation "labels omitted": the order named none; the relay refuses an empty array; nothing lost.
- Deviation "PR body headings folded into the os-dev order": prose layout only; both declaration lines are line-initial and the PR-body guards are green.
- Acceptance note "`tenancyPosture` / `audiencePosture` are closed enums, so a fourth posture fails an older client's parse instead of being stripped": the right call, not a flag. Both enums are the producer's own types (`TenancyPosture` from `@objectstack/spec/security`, `AudiencePosture` from `system/auth-config.zod.ts`), so a fourth value cannot be served without first moving the same spec constant the schema reuses; a `z.string()` would have thrown the vocabulary away. Consistent with the contract-first reading.
- Acceptance note "`termsUrl` / `privacyUrl` not URL-validated": matches the producer (`resolveLegalUrl` passes the trimmed value through unvalidated; the test fixture uses full URLs but the producer accepts a relative path).
- Out-of-scope finding (ui mirror `ui/packages/auth/src/types.ts` describes `sso` as "wired"): carried over from the card's own prose-only note, for the ui lane; not this PR's surface, nothing to escalate.
- Skills-docs: none, measured by the dev (`git grep` under `skills/`); the one `features.multiOrgEnabled` example in `skills/objectui/guides/auth-permissions.md` stays true under the declared boolean.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`, judged against the card's "Wanted" (declare each served key with a producer-accurate describe, in the #25292 / PR #29455 pattern; pin the registry to the schema) and against its first consumers (`@objectstack/client`'s re-exported `AuthFeaturesConfig`; the console readers of `deviceAuthorization`, `multiOrgEnabled`, `admin`, the legal links):

- **Holds.** Each describe was checked against the producer comment and the registry entry it restates: `multiOrgEnabled` (effective posture, false on `single` and on degraded; default-on semantics) matches `effectiveTenancyPosture()` and the registry's `default-on`; `tenancyPosture` and `audiencePosture` describe themselves as values, not gates, which is the producer's own ADR-0105 D1 / #11739 wording; `audiencePosture`'s "reported as invite_only when the configured value is off-vocabulary" is literally `ResolvedAudience.invalid`; `degradedTenancy` names `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY=1` as the producer does; `oidcProvider` "default-on alongside the MCP surface" is `resolveOidcProviderEnabled`; `deviceAuthorization`'s "the console device-approval page says device authorization is not enabled" is `DeviceAuthPage.tsx:77`; `admin` "forced on whenever SCIM is enabled" is ADR-0134 / `resolveScimEnabled`; `termsUrl` / `privacyUrl` describe the default public pages and the empty-string opt-out, which is `resolveLegalUrl`. No describe carries a tracker id (pinned by the test).
- **Attempts to break it:** (a) a served `tenancyPosture` of the legacy spelling `multi` — not reachable, `resolveTenancyPosture()` normalises it before returning and `TenancyService.posture` is typed on the same enum; (b) a served `audiencePosture` outside the vocabulary — not reachable, `getAudience()` coerces to `invite_only` for display; (c) `termsUrl` absent vs. default — the producer spreads the key only when defined, so `optional()` without a default is exactly right and a schema default would have invented a link the operator suppressed; (d) a `.default()` on any boolean — none added, so a client cannot read "on" for a key the server withheld (the CONTROL case pins this); (e) `lazySchema` Proxy and `.shape` in the pin — `.shape` is a deferred property access the Proxy forwards (the existing tests already read `AuthEndpointSchema.shape`), and the dev's ablation (rename one key → 3 failures incl. the set-equality pin, restored to the HEAD blob) shows the pin bites; (f) import cycle via the two new edges — none, both targets import only `zod`/`lazySchema`.
- **Should-fix (non-blocking, wording only):** the `termsUrl` / `privacyUrl` describes say the link is absent "when the operator set OS_TERMS_URL to an empty string"; `resolveLegalUrl` trims first, so a whitespace-only value suppresses the link too. "set to an empty or blank string" would be exact. Not a type or accept-set matter.
- No must-fix.
